# MO309485 bounded primary-source and mathematics review

**Verdict:** source and complete informal proof pass independent review; no exact prior settlement was located in the bounded primary literature reviewed. This permits source-faithful formalization with explicit credits and a bounded-search caveat. It does not establish novelty or historical priority.

The source is [Amdeberhan’s 2018 question](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/309485/an-eigenvalue-of-certain-family-of-matrices). The entire current body, all six comments, the corrected revision endpoint and timeline were read. There is one initial revision, no edits and no answer. The earlier error response from an invalid revisions route is not evidence of an empty history.

The faithful full answer is zero eigenvalue iff n>=1, with the source matrix on indices0..n and the second binomial set to zero when j<i. M_0=[3] is treated explicitly. The positive-n proof is essential; the boundary case is not a disproof campaign result. A complex-matrix statement is the standard characteristic-zero interpretation.

Lampe’s odd left nullvector (comment771010) and MTyson’s even right nullvector (771562) must be credited. The author’s September1 proof request refers to earlier proposals, while the even vector was posted September2. The uniform verification uses classical finite binomial identities. I independently checked both parities, omitted endpoints, nonzero-vector conditions and the n=0 distinction. The finite collaborator screen is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

## Primary papers and exact review scope

- [Fischer, Extreme DADASMs](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~kratt/esi3/Fischer.pdf): Dimension-halving section and adjoining definitions (presentation pages around40–45). Signed triangular binomial and reflection matrices with eigenvalue1/−1 are discussed for refined ASM/AST enumeration. The three-term source M_n, its two proposed nullvectors and full zero-eigenvalue classification were not identified in the reviewed section.

- [Bacher, Matrices related to the Pascal triangle (2001v2; journal2002)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0109013): Introduction, all theorem/proposition statements; Section1 determinant families, Section3 recursion setup, Section8 diagonal construction. Results concern shifted symmetric Pascal minors, polynomial perturbations and fixed Pascal or diagonal recursions. No theorem supplying the exact M_n singularity for all positive n or a complete source-family specialization was located.

- [Lunnon, The Pascal matrix (Fibonacci Quarterly15(3),1977,201–204)](https://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/15-3/lunnon.pdf): Entire four-page article. The symmetric matrix with entries C(i+j,i), its determinant1, inverse, positive minors and reciprocal eigenvalues are treated. That matrix is different from the three-term M_n; no exact source closure was located.

- [Molinari, Graphene nanocones and Pascal matrices (2022v2)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.14428): Runtime reviewed Pascal definitions and first determinant conjecture; collaborating Algebra worker independently read the entire15-page paper and recorded MO309485_MOLINARI_2022_SCOPE.md. Signed triangular/symmetric Pascal and honeycomb matrices differ from the source family. The full collaborator review found no exact M_n kernel/classification or supplied identification with the source parameters.

No exact statement or complete implication identifying those papers’ matrices with all source parameters was found. Both web engines were also checked for exact title/ID, matrix fragments and structural kernel/spectrum terms. These are bounded negative findings, not an exhaustive absence theorem. The relevant known vectors and classical mathematics must remain acknowledged.
